title: Parents' final break-up, the player piano and foster home
summary: His mother leaves with the car and his father greets him with a player piano; Fitzgerald sorts out the sequence, including a foster home in Cleveland before his grandfather's in Ypsilanti.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: some things happened there and then finally they decided to get together again in Lansing, Michigan, in 1932. Then they decided to break up and when they broke up, that day, when I came home from school my father had got a player piano and the dishes were in the sink and she took the car and when I walked in the door he was playing this player piano and I says, 'Good gracious, that's music,' and then things began to sink in a little more. So we were washing dishes together and he tried to explain to me that Mamma's gone and she took the car and whatnot, but we gonna make it. So, one thing I was good at was atheletics, so that took my mind off a lot of things, you know when you're young and impressionable, you know these things leave these deep scars. But I was a basketball player and I was a track man, even at that age.
Let's go back a little bit here for a minute, I just want to get the sequence of this straight. Now, you were born in Lansing and shortly after you were born, your mother and father split up...?
Yeah, married in Lansing...and they split up...
And your mother went to St. Louis?

No...I don't know where she went, but my father put me in a foster home so...one time I was in Cleveland and he said when he come to get me this woman had a racket. There was about eight or nine babies and I was skinny, I looked like I was gettin' ready to die... ha, ha, ha. So I don't remember anything, but this is what he told me, until I went to my grandfather's on my mother's side, Reverend Carr, in Ypsilanti.
About how old were you then?
I was about three or four years old.
So the foster home was before that, when you were really young?
Yeah, I didn't know nothing about that...
What were some of your actual first memories, like what comes to mind...
I remember that I was lonesome
